description: GNSS Performance Monitoring is a DLR website that compares the four worldwide satellite navigation systems, Galileo, GPS, GLONASS and BeiDou, using comparable metrics. It monitors the reliability and quality of navigation signals, detects deviations from the nominal state and shows indicators such as satellite visibility and geometry (dilution of precision), signal and service quality and positioning performance at selected stations, with observation and navigation data archived in a long-term database for trend analyses and comparisons. It covers the globe through data from a network of GNSS receiver stations. The site was developed and is operated by experts of DLR's Galileo Competence Center with the DLR Institutes of Software Technology, Communications and Navigation and Solar-Terrestrial Physics and the space operations facility, and was presented in a DLR article on 1 March 2024 as open to research, industry, society and policy users. It is free to view in a web browser without an account; DLR images are credited CC BY-NC-ND 3.0, and no data licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: the interactive application needs JavaScript and offers no documented bulk download or API on the pages read. It supports monitoring of service performance and resilience of satellite positioning that other infrastructures depend on, and hazard exposure studies of signal degradation; a related record is the DLR Ionosphere Monitoring and Prediction Center.
